payload.name: PreserveExplicitProcessDescriptions
payload.description: When a message contains an explicit description of the process, manner, or approach used for an action or creation, use this skill during extraction to preserve that description as a distinct memory fact.
content: During candidate extraction, if the speaker explicitly describes the process, manner, or approach of performing an action or creating something, preserve that explicit description as a separate memory fact, even when the message also contains emotional reactions or descriptions of the outcome.

Do not fold explicit process/manner statements into a summary of emotions or results. Keep them as distinct facts so the memory can answer future questions about how the speaker described the process.

solves: The diagnosed cause was extraction producing a summary of emotions and outcomes while omitting the speaker's explicit description of the creative process, leaving the memory unable to answer 'how was the process described'. The rule abstracts this by requiring explicit process/manner statements to be extracted as distinct facts; it applies to any future session where a speaker explicitly describes how an action or creation was performed, across any topic.
